own_solution.law: The secondary peak voltage is Vp = sqrt(2)Vm/4. With total conducting diode drop d = 1.4 V, the load voltage is max(Vp|sin(theta)| - d, 0). Setting alpha = asin(d/Vp), the average is [2Vp cos(alpha) - d(pi - 2alpha)]/pi.
assumptions: The stated ideal transformer and constant-drop diode models apply.
The bridge supplies a purely resistive load without smoothing.
The lamp has its own variable supply and no stated coupling to the transformer circuit.
An earlier run leaves no state affecting the present measurement.

notes: All governing relations, dimensions, strata and certified answers agree with the independent solution. Supply increments of 8, 14 and 21 V give average load voltages of 52.1762, 53.5265 and 55.1019 V, respectively. Each listed positive load resistance cancels from the average voltage under the stated models. The two explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve their numerical value and unit while changing attachment or measurement event.
